title: Microsoft 365 & Azure status
summary: Microsoft's public status: Azure, the Microsoft 365 admin center, Microsoft 365 consumer services and Azure incidents.
description:
Reads Microsoft's public status pages (status.cloud.microsoft and azure.status.microsoft) - no account or credential needed.

"Azure - status" and "Microsoft 365 - status" are Microsoft's overall verdicts; "Microsoft 365 consumer services" gives every consumer service (Outlook.com, OneDrive, Teams free ...) its own channel; "Azure - incidents (RSS)" counts open Azure incidents.

Note: the health of YOUR tenant's Exchange Online, Teams or SharePoint is only in the Microsoft 365 admin center (Service health) and needs a sign-in to Microsoft Graph; these templates show what Microsoft reports publicly - which is what matters when a whole region is down.
tags: Status page, Microsoft 365, Azure, Exchange Online, Microsoft
author: Matmon.eu

title: AWS status
summary: Amazon Web Services' public health feed: open events of every service and region.
description:
Reads the public AWS Health Dashboard feed - no AWS account needed.

"AWS - service health (RSS)" counts open AWS events (an item closes when AWS marks it resolved). The default feed covers every service in every region; to watch only what you use, change the sensor's target to that service's feed, e.g. https://status.aws.amazon.com/rss/ec2-eu-central-1.rss (the dashboard lists every feed).
author: Matmon.eu

title: Hornetsecurity status
summary: Hornetsecurity's public status page: every service, every service per location, and open incidents and maintenance.
description:
Reads Hornetsecurity's public status page (status.io API and its RSS feed) - no account or credential needed.

"Hornetsecurity - services" gives every service (Spam and Malware Protection, Email Encryption, Backup ...) its own channel; "Hornetsecurity - services by location" does the same per data centre ("Spam and Malware Protection - Germany - Frankfurt"); "Hornetsecurity - incidents (RSS)" counts open incidents and maintenance. A service that is not operational turns its channel - and the sensor - to warning or error, and the message names it.
tags: Status page, Hornetsecurity, E-mail security, Microsoft 365
author: Matmon.eu

title: GitHub status
summary: GitHub's public status: overall, every component (Git, Actions, Copilot ...) and incidents.
description:
Reads GitHub's public status page (www.githubstatus.com) - no account or credential needed.

"GitHub - overall status" is the page's own verdict (All Systems Operational / Minor / Major Outage / Maintenance) as one channel; "GitHub - components" gives every component its own channel, so a warning names what is affected; "GitHub - incidents (RSS)" counts open incidents and maintenance from the page's history feed.

Add the templates to a host or folder of your choice and create a sensor from each; the target is already set.

title: Matmon status
summary: Matmon's own services: Matmon Cloud, the matmon.eu website and the download feeds instances and agents update from.
description:
Watches what a Matmon installation relies on - no account or credential needed.

"Matmon Cloud - health" reads the cloud's health endpoint (cloud.matmon.eu/healthz): its own verdict and response time - if it fails, remote access, alert relay, SMS and cloud backups are affected. "Matmon Cloud - certificate" warns before the cloud's certificate runs out. "Matmon Cloud - sign-in page" checks the page people sign in on. "matmon.eu - website" checks the website. "Matmon - agent download feed" and "Matmon - Windows update feed" check the release files on GitHub that agents and Windows installations update from (how many agent packages there are, the size of the Windows package).

Add the templates to a host or folder of your choice and create a sensor from each; the target is already set.
author: Matmon.eu

title: pfSense (SNMP)
summary: pfSense over SNMP: reachability, CPU, load, memory, the packet filter's state table and the WAN interface's traffic.
description:
pfSense has no official API, so these templates read it over SNMP. On the firewall: Services > SNMP - enable it, set a community (or use SNMPv3 in the sensor), bind it to the LAN interface and tick the modules MibII, PF and UCD.

"pfSense - ping" checks that the firewall answers (latency, packet loss). "pfSense - system (SNMP)" reads uptime, idle CPU (warning below 15 %), the 1-minute load, real memory, whether the packet filter runs (critical when it does not) and the number of states. "pfSense - WAN interface (SNMP)" shows traffic and utilisation of one interface - set its interface index after adding it (index 1 is a guess; the SNMP walk in the sensor editor lists the interfaces). "pfSense - web interface certificate" warns before the certificate of the web interface runs out.

Add the templates to the host that is the firewall; they use the host's address. Put the SNMP community into an SNMP credential on the host (or type it into each sensor) - a template file never carries it.
author: Matmon.eu

title: STARFACE
summary: A STARFACE phone system: SIP answers, reachability, the web interface's certificate and - with SNMP switched on - CPU, load and memory.
description:
"STARFACE - SIP" sends a SIP OPTIONS request to port 5060 (UDP) and expects any answer - a 401 or 407 ("log in first") is a healthy answer from a phone system; silence is critical. "STARFACE - ping" checks reachability, latency and packet loss. "STARFACE - web interface certificate" warns before the certificate of the admin interface runs out.

"STARFACE - system (SNMP)" reads uptime, idle CPU (warning below 15 %), the 1-minute load and memory through the UCD-SNMP-MIB of the underlying Linux. It only works where SNMP is switched on for the STARFACE and the probe's address is allowed - leave it out otherwise. Use SIP over TCP in the sensor when the system only listens on TCP.

Add the templates to the host that is the STARFACE; they use the host's address. Trunk states, registered phones and calls are not read - that needs the STARFACE API.
author: Matmon.eu
